newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat's Romiti warns govt over severance pay.
newsitem.headline: Fiat's Romiti warns govt over severance pay.

text.p: Chairman of Italian industrial giant Fiat SpA Cesare Romiti on Friday warned the government it would face industrial opposition if severance pay was touched in its planned deficit-cutting mini-budget.

"When the budget's discussed one also hears talk of a levy on severance pay. I urge ministers to reflect deeply because this would then mean an estrangement of the Italian productive world from government," Romiti told a business meeting.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi, who has staked his political future on Italy being a founder member of the single European currency, has promised the mini-budget would be based on structural savings.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has indicated the package, due by the end of April, will raise around 14 trillion lire in a final bid to reduce the deficit to 3.0 percent of GDP.

Expected measures include transferring employee severance payment funds to Treasury coffers. Some analysts say Italy could move up to eight trillion lire into the Treasury with such a move despite opposition from some political allies and from companies which use the funds as cash flow.
Romiti noted that the country's employers' body Confindustria has said that a levy on severance pay would be very unjust. Furthermore, it would deprive companies, especially small ones, of funds.
"It is difficult to see how the taking on of a debt to workers could be considered as a reduction of the deficit to GDP ratio," Romiti added.
